prompt: Design a reusable A4 portrait grid for a 48-page cultural journal. Pages mix 900-word essays, full-bleed photography, captions, pull quotes, and short reviews. Provide the grid specification and two contrasting sample page plans.
must_observe: body measure and leading chosen before modules
margins account for binding and folios
limited picture spans with captions attached
two layouts share anchors but differ materially
long-text and full-bleed edge cases

prompt: Create a grid system for a 120-page annual report containing narrative chapters, financial tables, charts, case-study photographs, footnotes, and section openers. It must work in print and an accessible tagged PDF.
must_observe: table and chart label fit affects column choice
baseline and table-row rhythm are compatible
section openers use the same system with controlled variation
binding, trim, footnotes, and accessibility are addressed
production-ready measurements or tokens
must_avoid: decorative grid language without a specification
charts resized without regard to labels
print grid copied unchanged to screen

prompt: Define the layout grid for an operations dashboard at 1440px desktop, 1024px tablet, and 390px mobile. It contains a global status, six KPIs, two time-series charts, an alert queue, filters, and a detail drawer.
must_observe: separate breakpoint decisions
data-label and touch-target constraints
stable hierarchy and spacing logic across sizes
explicit column, gutter, margin, and vertical interval values
mobile prioritizes rather than shrinks
must_avoid: grid decisions detached from chart labels

prompt: Design a 24x36 inch event poster with one title, date, venue, sponsor line, and a single portrait. The organizer wants one dramatic element to break the grid while the information remains readable from across a room.
must_observe: viewing distance influences type and field size
simple grid appropriate to sparse content
exception preserves at least one anchor
hierarchy works without overlay
sponsor line remains legible and subordinate
must_avoid: exception justified only as visual interest

prompt: Design a facing-page grid for a bilingual English/German architecture catalog. German copy can be 25 percent longer. Each project has plans, photographs, captions, credits, and page numbers.
must_observe: language expansion stress test
facing-page and binding relationship
paired or coordinated baselines
plans and photos use a limited span family
captions and credits remain attached
must_avoid: independent left and right pages with no spread logic

prompt: Create a modular grid for a museum exhibition across three walls, a central plinth, and directional signs. Visitors approach from two entrances; labels must work for standing adults, children, and wheelchair users.
must_observe: wall dimensions, sight lines, circulation, and viewing distance
relationship among text, image, objects, and signs
accessible height bands rather than one average eye level
grid extends coherently into three dimensions
lighting and material constraints

prompt: Audit a polished landing page whose cards appear almost aligned, body lines are very long, captions drift below images, mobile spacing uses many one-off values, and the hero intentionally crosses columns. Return prioritized findings and repairs.
must_observe: separates symptoms from structural causes
prioritizes readability and systemic drift
gives measurable repairs
evaluates the hero exception by benefit and anchors
states what should remain unchanged
must_avoid: forcing the hero back into the grid automatically
one-off pixel fixes for every card

prompt: Use a standard 12-column Bootstrap-style grid for a single-column poetry chapbook with very short lines, generous pauses, occasional notes, and no images. Define the final layout.
must_observe: challenges or simplifies the requested preset with clear reasoning
derives a sparse system from poetry, notes, and pacing
white space treated as content-bearing
maintains implementable anchors
must_avoid: twelve equal columns used merely because requested

prompt: Create one grid logic for a research institute across letterhead, a two-page brief, a 16:9 slide, a social card, and a web article. Explain what stays invariant and what must change.
must_observe: shared interval, alignment, hierarchy, or span logic
format-specific margins and column counts
small-format simplification
web reading measure and responsive behavior
identity comes from relationships, not identical coordinates
must_avoid: logo placement as the only invariant
social card crowded with brief content

prompt: A designer proposes a 24-column by 20-row grid for a simple four-page product brochure with one paragraph, three features, a specification table, and four images per page. Recommend and specify a better system.
must_observe: tests whether the fine mesh solves a real need
chooses fewer useful divisions
spec table and images influence spans
shows multiple compositions remain possible
explains reduced arbitrariness and implementation cost
must_avoid: choosing a simpler grid without measurements
making every image identical without considering importance

prompt: Review a component-based editorial page system. Some cards have no image, headlines range from 20 to 110 characters, captions may be two lines, and translated body copy expands by 30 percent. Identify tests and rule changes needed before launch.
must_observe: longest and missing-content states
baseline and card alignment behavior
caption and translation expansion
responsive reflow rules
distinguishes content constraints from grid defects
must_avoid: assuming translation can use smaller type
